The main takeaway from our work is that
the oncogenic properties of myelobastosis-associated virus are not restricted to the avian species.
the oncogenic potential of a virus can be dissected into two independent functions: one that promotes the development of the tumor and another that is required for the maintenance of tumor cells.
myeloblatosis-associated virus is not only the first retrovirus to induce a tumor but also the first one to be shown to be able to induce two different tumors in the same species.
